defect: B683: sideband callback delivery resumed the origin thread (thread/resume) before deciding turn/start vs turn/steer; against the actual production owner thread (very large history) that thread/resume round trip repeatedly exhausted the mux's bounded 45-second sideband deadline. Batch de917c12b5b849308db7ae562fa59a17 reached attempts>=8, hard_failure_count=1, last_failure_kind=busy/not_ready while the durable event stayed parked forever, never delivered.
repair: SidebandCallbackClient delivery (deliver_callback/deliver_callback_batch -> _deliver_turn) no longer sends thread/resume or turn/steer at all. It issues exactly one turn/start directly against the uniquely resolved live mux owner for the exact origin_thread_id, using the existing deterministic clientUserMessageId and callback prompt. A successful synchronous TurnStartResponse.turn.id is the only delivery acknowledgement -- the App Server's own turn/start response is the atomic concurrency authority. An active/busy/activeTurnNotSteerable/already-in-progress rejection (classified by _is_sideband_turn_start_busy_rejection against both the free-text message and the CodexErrorInfo.activeTurnNotSteerable structured shape) raises SidebandThreadBusyError, a BusyThreadError subclass that durably parks via defer_batch_busy without consuming the bounded hard-failure budget. A malformed/denied/protocol-shaped rejection (missing result.turn.id, an unrelated error, an unauthorized/rejected sideband envelope) still raises the base AppServerError and retains the existing bounded fail_batch_transient retry/dead-letter path. thread_resume/turn_steer remain available as standalone SidebandCallbackClient primitives (used directly by owner-resolution/auth diagnostics and tests) but are never invoked by the delivery path. The subprocess transport (AppServerClient, select_steer_target, resume-decides-steer-or-start) is entirely unchanged.
